messages.content: Change the settings of my air conditioner. Set it to cool mode with a target temperature of 22 degrees Celsius. Enable the power save mode and set the high wind strength. Start in 1 hour and 30 minutes from now? For everything else

function.name: ThinQ_Connect
function.description: Sends a command to control an appliance, allowing only a single value to be sent in one call. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

body.description: A dictionary containing the parameters for the appliance command.

airConJobMode.description: The current job mode of the air conditioner.

windStrength.description: The strength of the air flow.

monitoringEnabled.description: Whether air quality sensor monitoring is enabled.

airCleanOperationMode.description: The operation mode for the air cleaning function.

airConOperationMode.description: The operation mode for the air conditioner, indicating if it is turned on or off.

powerSaveEnabled.description: Whether power save mode is enabled to conserve energy.

targetTemperature.description: The target temperature to set for the appliance, in degrees Celsius.

relativeHourToStop.description: The number of hours from the current time when the appliance should stop. If set to null, the appliance will not be scheduled to stop.

relativeMinuteToStop.description: The number of minutes from the current time when the appliance should stop. If set to null, the appliance will not be scheduled to stop.

relativeHourToStart.description: The number of hours from the current time when the appliance should start. If set to null, the appliance will not be scheduled to start.

relativeMinuteToStart.description: The number of minutes from the current time when the appliance should start. If set to null, the appliance will not be scheduled to start.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to change settings of their air conditioner. They want to set it to cool mode with a target temperature of 22°C. Enable power save mode and set high wind strength. Start in 1 hour and 30 minutes from now. For everything else, presumably keep defaults or leave unspecified.

We need to use the ThinQ_Connect function. We need to provide a JSON body with the relevant fields. The function expects a dictionary with keys: airConJobMode, windStrength, monitoringEnabled, airCleanOperationMode, airConOperationMode, powerSaveEnabled, targetTemperature, relativeHourToStop, relativeMinuteToStop, relativeHourToStart, relativeMinuteToStart.

We need to set airConJobMode to "COOL". windStrength to "HIGH". powerSaveEnabled to true. targetTemperature to 22. relativeHourToStart to 1. relativeMinuteToStart to 30. For everything else, we can omit them or set to defaults. The function signature says default values but we don't need to include them. So we can just include the ones we want to set. But we might need to include airConOperationMode? The user didn't specify turning on or off. But maybe we need to set airConOperationMode to "POWER_ON"? The user wants to start in 1 hour and 30 minutes from now. That implies we want to schedule a start. The function has relativeHourToStart and relativeMinuteToStart. We set those. We also need to set airConOperationMode? The function's description: "The operation mode for the air conditioner, indicating if it is turned on or off." Default: POWER_OFF. If we want to schedule a start, we probably need to set airConOperationMode to "POWER_ON". But the user didn't explicitly say to turn it on. But they said "Start in 1 hour and 30 minutes from now?" That implies we want to schedule a start. So we set airConOperationMode to "POWER_ON".

Also, we might need to set airCleanOperationMode? Not necessary. We can leave it as default STOP. Also monitoringEnabled default false. So we can skip.

Thus the body:

{
  airConJobMode: "COOL",
  windStrength: "HIGH",
  powerSaveEnabled: true,
  targetTemperature: 22,
  airConOperationMode: "POWER_ON",
  relativeHourToStart: 1,
  relativeMinuteToStart: 30
}

We can also include relativeHourToStop and relativeMinuteToStop as null or omit. The function signature says default null. So we can omit.

Thus we call ThinQ_Connect with body containing those fields.

We need to produce a JSON object with the body key mapping to the dictionary. The function expects a dictionary with a key "body" mapping to the dictionary. So we need to call the function with argument: { body: { ... } }

Thus we produce a function call.
